questions.knowledgeNote: Double-angle backwards: 2x^2-1 is cos2t in disguise; the principal range forces x >= 0.
questions.question: Q4(a). Prove that 2cos-1x = cos-1(2x^2-1).
questions.solution: Put t = cos-1x in [0, pi], so x = cost. Then 2x^2-1 = 2cos^2t-1 = cos2t. For 2t to be the principal value we need 2t in [0, pi], i.e. t in [0, pi/2], i.e. x >= 0; then cos-1(2x^2-1) = 2t = 2cos-1x. Proved (valid for 0 <= x <= 1; the book states it without the hypothesis).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q4(a); book pp167-168 = PDF pp194-195

questions.knowledgeNote: Triple-angle backwards: 4x^3-3x is cos3t; needs 3t inside [0, pi], i.e. x >= 1/2.
questions.question: Q4(b). Prove that 3cos-1x = cos-1(4x^3-3x).
questions.solution: Put t = cos-1x in [0, pi], so x = cost. Then 4x^3-3x = 4cos^3t-3cost = cos3t. For 3t to be the principal value we need 3t in [0, pi], i.e. t in [0, pi/3], i.e. x in [1/2, 1]; then cos-1(4x^3-3x) = 3t = 3cos-1x. Proved (valid for 1/2 <= x <= 1).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q4(b); book pp167-168 = PDF pp194-195

questions.knowledgeNote: tan3t expansion with tant = x; needs 3t inside (-pi/2, pi/2), i.e. |x| < 1/sqrt(3).
questions.question: Q4(c). Prove that 3tan-1x = tan-1((3x-x^3)/(1-3x^2)).
questions.solution: Put t = tan-1x in (-pi/2, pi/2), so x = tant. Then tan3t = (3tant-tan^3t)/(1-3tan^2t) = (3x-x^3)/(1-3x^2). For 3t to be the principal value we need 3t in (-pi/2, pi/2), i.e. |x| < 1/sqrt(3); then tan-1 of the fraction is 3t = 3tan-1x. Proved (valid for |x| < 1/sqrt(3)).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q4(c); book pp167-168 = PDF pp194-195

questions.knowledgeNote: Both sides equal sqrt(1-t^2): each cofunction lands on the non-negative branch.
questions.question: Q4(d). Prove that sin(arccos t) = cos(arcsin t).
questions.solution: arccos t lies in [0, pi] where sine is non-negative, so sin(arccos t) = +sqrt(1-t^2). arcsin t lies in [-pi/2, pi/2] where cosine is non-negative, so cos(arcsin t) = +sqrt(1-t^2). Both equal sqrt(1-t^2). Proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q4(d); book pp167-168 = PDF pp194-195

questions.knowledgeNote: Direct cos2t with cost = t: no range subtlety since 2t^2-1 always lies in [-1, 1].
questions.question: Q4(e). Prove that cos(2arccost) = 2t^2-1.
questions.solution: Put u = arccost, so cosu = t. Then cos2u = 2cos^2u-1 = 2t^2-1. Proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q4(e); book pp167-168 = PDF pp194-195

questions.knowledgeNote: sin2t = 2sintcost with sint = x and cost = +sqrt(1-x^2) on the sin-1 range. (HSEB 2057)
questions.question: Q4(f). Prove that sin(2sin-1x) = 2x.sqrt(1-x^2). (HSEB 2057)
questions.solution: Put t = sin-1x in [-pi/2, pi/2], so sint = x and cost = +sqrt(1-x^2). Then sin2t = 2sintcost = 2x.sqrt(1-x^2). Proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q4(f) (HSEB 2057); book pp167-168 = PDF pp194-195

questions.knowledgeNote: cos(A+B) = cosAcosB-sinAsinB with cosA = sqrt(1-u^2), sinB = sqrt(1-v^2): test u = v = 0 gives cos(pi/2) = 0. (T.U. 2049)
questions.question: Q4(g). Prove that cos(sin-1u+cos-1v) = v.sqrt(1-u^2)-u.sqrt(1-v^2). (T.U. 2049)
questions.solution: Put A = sin-1u (sinA = u, cosA = +sqrt(1-u^2)) and B = cos-1v (cosB = v, sinB = +sqrt(1-v^2)). Then cos(A+B) = cosAcosB-sinAsinB = v.sqrt(1-u^2)-u.sqrt(1-v^2). Check u = v = 0: LHS = cos(0+pi/2) = 0, RHS = 0. Proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q4(g) (T.U. 2049); book pp167-168 = PDF pp194-195

questions.knowledgeNote: Sum formula with positive denominator 1-1/35: the sum stays acute.
questions.question: Q4(h). Prove that tan-1(1/5)+tan-1(1/7) = tan-1(6/17).
questions.solution: (1/5+1/7)/(1-(1/5)(1/7)) = (12/35)/(34/35) = 12/34 = 6/17. Both angles are acute and their product 1/35 < 1, so the sum is the acute angle tan-1(6/17). Proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q4(h); book pp167-168 = PDF pp194-195

questions.knowledgeNote: Telescoping in disguise: each RHS term is a difference of two tan-1, and the middle terms cancel.
questions.question: Q4(i). Prove that tan-1a-tan-1c = tan-1((a-b)/(1+ab))+tan-1((b-c)/(1+bc)).
questions.solution: Where defined (ab, bc > -1), tan-1((a-b)/(1+ab)) = tan-1a-tan-1b and tan-1((b-c)/(1+bc)) = tan-1b-tan-1c by the difference formula. Adding: the tan-1b terms cancel, leaving tan-1a-tan-1c. Proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q4(i); book pp167-168 = PDF pp194-195

questions.knowledgeNote: tan(A-B) with tanA = u, tanB = v: one line.
questions.question: Q4(j). Prove that tan(arctanu-arctanv) = (u-v)/(1+uv).
questions.solution: Put A = arctanu, B = arctanv, so tanA = u and tanB = v. Then tan(A-B) = (tanA-tanB)/(1+tanAtanB) = (u-v)/(1+uv). Proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q4(j); book pp167-168 = PDF pp194-195 (image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: (x+x^3)/(1-x^4) simplifies by cancelling (1+x^2): the x^3 term is there to make this happen. (HSEB 2052)
questions.question: Q4(k). Prove that tan(2tan-1x) = 2tan(tan-1x+tan-1x^3). (HSEB 2052)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q4(k) (HSEB 2052); book pp167-168 = PDF pp194-195 (image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: tan(A+B+C) = (s1-xyz)/(1-s2): expand once, quote forever. (HSEB 2055)
questions.question: Q4(l). Prove that tan-1x+tan-1y+tan-1z = tan-1((x+y+z-xyz)/(1-xy-yz-zx)). (HSEB 2055)
questions.solution: Put A = tan-1x, B = tan-1y, C = tan-1z. Then tan(A+B+C) = (tanA+tanB+tanC-tanAtanBtanC)/(1-(tanAtanB+tanBtanC+tanCtanA)) = (x+y+z-xyz)/(1-xy-yz-zx). Taking tan-1 (principal branch where defined) gives the formula. Proved. (Statement via image read of the cut-off line.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q4(l) (HSEB 2055); book p167 = PDF p194 (image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: First two angles combine to cos-1(16/65); the third is its complement. (HSEB 2053)
questions.question: Q4(m). Prove that sin-1(4/5)+sin-1(5/13)+sin-1(16/65) = pi/2. (HSEB 2053)
questions.solution: sin of the first two summed: (4/5)(12/13)+(3/5)(5/13) = 48/65+15/65 = 63/65; cos: (3/5)(12/13)-(4/5)(5/13) = 36/65-20/65 = 16/65 > 0. So their sum is the acute angle with cosine 16/65, i.e. cos-1(16/65). Adding sin-1(16/65) gives pi/2. Proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q4(m) (HSEB 2053); book p167 = PDF p194 (image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Put sqrt(x) = tant: both fractions become cos2t and sin2t with 2t in [0, pi/2]. (T.U. 2055 S, HSEB 2054)
questions.question: Q4(n). Prove that tan-1(sqrt(x)) = (1/2)cos-1((1-x)/(1+x)) = (1/2)sin-1(2sqrt(x)/(1+x)). (T.U. 2055 S, HSEB 2054)
questions.solution: For 0 <= x < 1 put sqrt(x) = tant with t in [0, pi/4). Then (1-tan^2t)/(1+tan^2t) = cos2t with 2t in [0, pi/2), so cos-1 of it is 2t; and 2tant/(1+tan^2t) = sin2t, so sin-1 of it is 2t. Halving gives t = tan-1(sqrt(x)) in both cases. Proved.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q4(n) (T.U. 2055 S, HSEB 2054); book p168 = PDF p195 (image read)

questions.question: Q5(a). Find cos(sin-1(4/5)+tan-1(5/12)). (HSEB 2054, 2055)
questions.solution: sinA = 4/5 gives cosA = 3/5; tanB = 5/12 gives sinB = 5/13, cosB = 12/13. cos(A+B) = cosAcosB-sinAsinB = (3/5)(12/13)-(4/5)(5/13) = 36/65-20/65 = 16/65. Matches the printed Answers key (p169): 16/65.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q5(a) (HSEB 2054, 2055); book p168 = PDF p195 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: sin(60deg+A) with sinA = 3/5, cosA = 4/5. (T.U. 2053 H)
questions.question: Q5(b). Find sin(cos-1(1/2)+sin-1(3/5)). (T.U. 2053 H)
questions.solution: cos-1(1/2) = 60deg; sinA = 3/5 gives cosA = 4/5. sin(60deg+A) = sin60cosA+cos60sinA = (sqrt(3)/2)(4/5)+(1/2)(3/5) = (4sqrt(3)+3)/10. Matches the printed Answers key (p169): (4sqrt(3)+3)/10.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q5(b) (T.U. 2053 H); book p168 = PDF p195 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: tanA = 3/4, tanB = 12/5: the difference formula gives a negative over a positive.
questions.question: Q5(c). Find tan(arccos(4/5)-arcsin(12/13)).
questions.solution: cosA = 4/5 gives tanA = 3/4; sinB = 12/13 gives tanB = 12/5. tan(A-B) = (3/4-12/5)/(1+(3/4)(12/5)) = (-33/20)/(56/20) = -33/56. (This key row is illegible in the key scan; verified by substitution: arctan(-33/56) ~ -30.5deg and arccos(4/5)-arcsin(12/13) ~ 36.87-67.38 = -30.5deg.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q5(c); book p168 = PDF p195 (image read); substitution-verified (key row illegible)

questions.knowledgeNote: Direct difference formula with second argument 2y. (HSEB 2053)
questions.question: Q5(d). Find tan(tan-1x-tan-12y). i.e. tan(tan-1x-tan-1(2y)). (HSEB 2053)
questions.solution: By the tan difference formula with arguments x and 2y: (x-2y)/(1+x.2y) = (x-2y)/(1+2xy). Matches the printed Answers key (p169): (x-2y)/(1+2xy).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q5(d) (HSEB 2053); book p168 = PDF p195 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: Product 3.(1/3) = 1: complementary acute angles sum to pi/2.
questions.question: Q5(e). Find tan-13+tan-1(1/3). i.e. tan-1(3)+tan-1(1/3).
questions.solution: Both angles are acute and their tangents multiply to 3.(1/3) = 1, so they are complementary: sum = pi/2 (tan-1(3) ~ 71.57deg, tan-1(1/3) ~ 18.43deg). (The key scan shows the value with the /2 cut off; the exact value is pi/2.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q5(e); book p168 = PDF p195 (image read); exact value pi/2 (key scan cut off)

questions.knowledgeNote: arccos(-t) = pi-arccost: the pi survives while the rest collapses to pi/2.
questions.question: Q5(f). Find arcsint-arccos(-t). i.e. sin-1t-cos-1(-t).
questions.solution: arccos(-t) = pi-arccost. So sin-1t-cos-1(-t) = sin-1t+cos-1t-pi = pi/2-pi = -pi/2. (The key shows a negative value here; the exact value is -pi/2.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q5(f); book p168 = PDF p195 (image read); exact value -pi/2

questions.knowledgeNote: Equal inverse values mean the 45-degree angle: both are pi/4, so x = sqrt(2)/2.
questions.question: Q6(a). Solve cos-1x-sin-1x = 0.
questions.solution: cos-1x = sin-1x =: t. Then x = cost = sint with t in [0, pi/2], so t = pi/4 and x = sqrt(2)/2 = 1/sqrt(2). Check: pi/4-pi/4 = 0. (The key scan reads 1/2 with the root sign lost; the exact value is 1/sqrt(2).)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q6(a); book p168 = PDF p195 (image read); exact value 1/sqrt(2)

questions.knowledgeNote: Difference zero means the two complementary angles are equal: each pi/4.
questions.question: Q6(b). Solve tan-1x-cot-1x = 0.
questions.solution: tan-1x = cot-1x; since they sum to pi/2, each is pi/4, so x = tan(pi/4) = 1. Check: pi/4-pi/4 = 0. Matches the printed Answers key (p169): x = 1.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q6(b); book p168 = PDF p195 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: One angle, two trig ratios: sin = x/2 and cos = x force x^2/4+x^2 = 1. (HSEB 2052)
questions.question: Q6(c). Solve sin-1(x/2) = cos-1x. (HSEB 2052)
questions.solution: Let the common value be t: sint = x/2 and cost = x. Then x^2/4+x^2 = 1, i.e. x^2 = 4/5, and x >= 0 (t in [0, pi/2] from the ranges), so x = 2/sqrt(5). Check: sin-1(1/sqrt(5)) = cos-1(2/sqrt(5)) ~ 26.57deg. Matches the printed Answers key (p169): x = 2/sqrt(5).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q6(c) (HSEB 2052); book p168 = PDF p195 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: Equal principal values with the same cosine: x = 1/(2x). (HSEB 2051)
questions.question: Q6(d). Solve cos-1x = cos-1(1/(2x)). (HSEB 2051)
questions.solution: Both sides are principal values in [0, pi], so x = 1/(2x), i.e. x^2 = 1/2, i.e. x = +-1/sqrt(2). Both satisfy |1/(2x)| = 1/sqrt(2) <= 1. Matches the printed Answers key (p169): x = +-1/sqrt(2).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q6(d) (HSEB 2051); book p168 = PDF p195 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: Take tan of both sides: 2x = 2x/(1-x^2) has only the trivial root.
questions.question: Q6(e). Solve tan-12x = 2tan-1x. i.e. tan-1(2x) = 2tan-1x.
questions.solution: Taking tan: 2x = 2x/(1-x^2). Either x = 0 or 1-x^2 = 1, which also gives x = 0. So x = 0 (check: 0 = 0). Matches the printed Answers key (p169): x = 0.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q6(e); book p168 = PDF p195 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: cos-12x = sin-1x forces 2x = +sqrt(1-x^2): squaring admits a negative ghost.
questions.question: Q6(f). Solve cos-1x+cos-1(2x) = pi/2.
questions.solution: cos-1(2x) = pi/2-cos-1x = sin-1x. Taking cos: 2x = cos(sin-1x) = +sqrt(1-x^2), which needs x >= 0. Squaring: 4x^2 = 1-x^2, i.e. x^2 = 1/5, i.e. x = 1/sqrt(5) (x = -1/sqrt(5) gives LHS = 3pi/2, extraneous). Check x = 1/sqrt(5): sum is pi/2. The printed key lists +-1/sqrt(5); only +1/sqrt(5) satisfies the equation (flagged).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q6(f); book p168 = PDF p195 (image read); exact x = 1/sqrt(5), negative root extraneous (key overlists)

questions.knowledgeNote: The complement of sin-1x is cos-1x itself: 1-x must equal x.
questions.question: Q6(g). Solve sin-1x+cos-1(1-x) = pi/2.
questions.solution: cos-1(1-x) = pi/2-sin-1x = cos-1x (since pi/2-sin-1x = cos-1x). Both sides principal values gives 1-x = x, i.e. x = 1/2. Check: pi/6+pi/3 = pi/2.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q6(g); book p168 = PDF p195 (image read); substitution-verified

questions.knowledgeNote: Both exotic forms are double-angle masks: 2tan-1a minus 2tan-1b. (HSEB 2053)
questions.question: Q6(h). If sin-1(2a/(1+a^2))-cos-1((1-b^2)/(1+b^2)) = 2tan-1x, show that x = (a-b)/(1+ab). (HSEB 2053)
questions.solution: sin-1(2a/(1+a^2)) = 2tan-1a and cos-1((1-b^2)/(1+b^2)) = 2tan-1b. So 2tan-1a-2tan-1b = 2tan-1x, i.e. tan-1x = tan-1a-tan-1b = tan-1((a-b)/(1+ab)), giving x = (a-b)/(1+ab). Shown. (The key row is garbled but consistent with (h) x = (a-b)/(1+ab).)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q6(h) (HSEB 2053); book p168 = PDF p195 (image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Sum formula: A+B and 1-AB turn out equal (both 6/7 at the roots), so the sum is genuinely pi/4.
questions.question: Q6(i). Solve tan-1((x-1)/(x-2))+tan-1((x+1)/(x+2)) = tan-1(1).
questions.solution: With A = (x-1)/(x-2), B = (x+1)/(x+2): A+B = (2x^2-4)/(x^2-4), 1-AB = -3/(x^2-4). A+B = 1-AB gives 2x^2-4 = -3, i.e. x^2 = 1/2, x = +-1/sqrt(2). At both roots A+B = 6/7 > 0 and 1-AB = 6/7 > 0, so the sum is genuinely pi/4. Both valid. Matches the printed Answers key (p169): x = +-1/sqrt(2).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q6(i); book p168 = PDF p195 (image read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: 5x = 1-6x^2 gives x = 1/6 and x = -1, but only 1/6 keeps A+B and 1-AB positive.
questions.question: Q6(j). Solve tan-12x+tan-13x = pi/4. i.e. tan-1(2x)+tan-1(3x) = pi/4.
questions.solution: (2x+3x)/(1-6x^2) = 1 gives 6x^2+5x-1 = 0, i.e. (6x-1)(x+1) = 0, so x = 1/6 or x = -1. x = 1/6: A+B = 5/6 > 0, 1-AB = 5/6 > 0, sum genuinely pi/4, valid. x = -1: LHS = -3pi/4, extraneous. True solution x = 1/6; the printed key lists both roots without the domain check (flagged).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q6(j); book p168 = PDF p195 (image read); true x = 1/6, x = -1 extraneous (key overlists)

questions.knowledgeNote: 1/(2+sqrt(3)) = 2-sqrt(3) = tan15deg: triple it to land on 45deg.
questions.question: Q6(k). Solve 3tan-1(1/(2+sqrt(3)))-tan-1(1/x) = tan-1(1/3).
questions.solution: 1/(2+sqrt(3)) = 2-sqrt(3) = tan15deg, so 3tan-1(1/(2+sqrt(3))) = 3.15deg = 45deg = pi/4. Then tan-1(1/x) = pi/4-tan-1(1/3) = tan-1((1-1/3)/(1+1/3)) = tan-1(1/2), so 1/x = 1/2, i.e. x = 2. Check in the original: pi/4-tan-1(1/2) = tan-1(1/3) since (1-1/2)/(1+1/2) = 1/3. Matches the printed Answers key (p169): x = 2.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q6(k); book p168 = PDF p195 (image read); matches key
